speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for seeing me. To better understand your dizziness, can you describe the specific sensations you feel, such as spinning, lightheadedness, or a feeling of unsteadiness? Also, how long do these episodes typically last?

speaker: Patient
text: 70-year-old woman. The patient presents with sudden episodes of dizziness that are position dependent. She describes experiencing a false sensation of motion and occasional spinning, indicative of vertigo. She denies any recent illnesses, injuries, or significant changes in health status, apart from age-related hearing loss (presbycusis).

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for that detailed description; the position-dependent nature of your episodes is very telling. Has this dizziness been associated with any changes in your hearing, such as ringing in the ears (tinnitus) or a feeling of fullness in your ear?

REQUEST TEST: Audiometry

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Audiometry: Bilateral high-frequency sensorineural hearing loss, consistent with presbycusis. No sudden drops in hearing indicative of Meniere's disease or labyrinthitis.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Doctor: Given your age and the specific nature of the spinning sensation triggered by head movements, have you noticed any recent falls or a specific trigger like rolling over in bed or looking up? Also, do you experience any nausea or vomiting during these episodes?

REQUEST TEST: Dix-Hallpike Maneuver
REQUEST IMAGES: MRI_Brain

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Dix-Hallpike Maneuver: Positive for right-sided horizontal nystagmus when moving from sitting to supine position, suggestive of BPPV. MRI_Brain: No evidence of central lesions or infarcts that would suggest central causes of vertigo.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV).
